result.owner_identity: observed DOS far address 50F6:3862 from S09 original disassembly and current source references
result.blocker: LoadGame and SaveGame pass local name buffers to FileSelect without a capacity argument. LoadGame does not initialize its name local before FileSelect first reads it; FileSelect forms and copies complete paths using unbounded string operations. No independently grounded maximum full-string input or destination extent was found.

source_facts.fact: The symbol is declared unsized; LoadGame and SaveGame use 100-byte local names and unbounded far copies; FileSelect has no capacity parameter, reads the incoming name, and builds/copies paths without a bound.
The file-selection editor's maxLen=9 limits typed input to eight characters; that bounds only the typed basename.

LoadGame initializes its ok local, then calls FileSelect at S09:35F5:0052 with the BP-0x6c local and performs no initialization of that name local first. After preliminary chdir/current-drive setup, FileSelect's first name access reads *name at S09:35F5:0402. SaveGame calls FileSelect at S09:35F5:0237 with BP-0x6a on the new-file route without prior initialization; its reuse-last route first copies the global into that local. Both successful dialog paths copy full name strings to the far global.

prior_target_evidence.recorded_fact: fd_50F6_3862 and its unsized filename buffer remain open; no capacity was inferred.

win16_read_only_review.finding: ClearLastFileName writes editBufInvalidFlag[1834] = 0; it contains no remembered filename declaration. The Win16 disassembly cards label _LoadGame, _SaveGame and _FileSelect, but give no global declaration or capacity.
